### [S034.U1] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.11 REQUIREMENTS FOR MASS CONCRETE
- A. Mass concrete clauses shall apply to concrete used in Mat Foundations and should be considered for footings greater than 1.0 m thick. Same materials and proportioning as normal weight structural concrete, except use moderate heat of hydration, moderate sulphate resistance cement, water reducing retarding admixture, and crushed ice if necessary to maintain required temperature.

1. Retardation: Minimum 3 hours.
2. Temperature: Maximum 21° C at point of deposit.

### [S045.U1] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.5 REINFORCEMENT
- A. General: Clean reinforcement of loose rust and mill scale, earth, and other materials that reduce or destroy bond with concrete. Where vapor barrier is required, avoid cutting or puncturing vapor barrier during reinforcement placement and concreting operations.
- B. Position, support, and secure reinforcement against displacement by formwork, construction, or concrete placement operations. Locate and support reinforcing with metal chairs, runners, bolsters, spacers, and hangers, as required. Place reinforcement to obtain the required minimum coverages for concrete protection. Arrange, space, and securely tie bar supports together with (1.6mm) wire to hold reinforcement accurately in position during concrete placement operations. Set wire ties so that twisted ends are directed away from exposed concrete surfaces.

### [S048.U1] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.5 REINFORCEMENT > F. Cover to Reinforcement
1. Reinforcement shall have concrete cover and the thickness of such cover shall be as specified in the Drawings or as directed by the ER.
- G. Fixing in position
1. Correctly cut and bent bars shall be accurately placed in position as detailed in the Drawings. Unless otherwise specified by the ER, reinforcement shall be positioned within the tolerance as under:

### [S048.U2] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.5 REINFORCEMENT > F. Cover to Reinforcement > G. Fixing in position
- a. for effective depth 200 mm or less  10 mm
- b. for effective depth more than 200 mm  15 mm
2. But in no case shall the cover be reduced by more than 5 mm of that specified. There shall be no compromise on cover for foundation work.
3. Reinforcing bars shall be held in position during the placing of concrete by use of PVC or concrete cover blocks ( made of equal / of higher grade strength of well-cured concrete in use) steel chair spacers, steel hangers, supporting wires, etc. and secured by tying with an annealed binding wire of 16 to 18 gauge as approved by the ER.

### [S048.U4] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.5 REINFORCEMENT > F. Cover to Reinforcement > G. Fixing in position
5. Binding wire used shall conform to IS 280.
- H. Welded joints or mechanical connections
1. Welded joints or mechanical connections in reinforcement may be used but in all cases or important connections, tests shall be made to prove that the joints are of the full strength of the connected bars. Welding of reinforcement shall be done in accordance with IS recommendation.
2. Where reinforcement bars are bent aside at construction joints and afterwards bent

- back into their original position, care shall be taken to ensure that at no time is the radius of the bend allowed to be less than 4 bar diameters in case of plain mild steel or 6 bar diameters for deformed bars. Care shall be taken when bending back bars to ensure that the concrete around them is not damaged / disturbed.
3. Welding rods used shall conform to IS 814: covered electrodes for metal arc welding of structural steel. Work shall be carried out by a certified welder. Samples from Work site shall be taken at regular intervals and tested. Frequency and number of samples shall be as directed by the ER.

### [S049.U2] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE
- B. Cement Concrete.
1. This shall be classified as plain cement concrete or reinforced cement concrete. Plain cement concrete shall be used in leveling courses under foundations, floors, copings etc. Reinforced cement concrete shall be used typically at all locations.
- a. Concrete shall be classified by its compressive strength at the 28th day. The concrete grades shall be as designated in table 2 of IS 456 and are given as ready reference in Table - 4.

### [S049.U3] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > B. Cement Concrete.
- b. It shall be the responsibility of the Contractor to carry out design mixes and approval of the same shall be obtained from the ER at least 35 days in advance from the actual pouring of concrete at site in the permanent Work. The basic aim of mix design shall be to find the most economic proportion of cement, aggregates and water which will give the desired strength of concrete, proper workability and durability. Also it is important that the mix should be easily worked with the help of equipment available at site. The operations involved at site are, measurement of materials, their mixing, placing, compacting, finishing required and curing. The design shall be carried out strictly to IS specifications and IS code practice 456, SP 23 and SP 24.

### [S049.U4] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > B. Cement Concrete.
- c. The Contractor shall ensure that the minimum cement content per cubic

- meter of reinforced concrete should not be less than that stipulated in table 23, 24, 25 and 26 of SP 23 and Table 5 and Table 6 herein.
- d. For expected strength of cubes tested on the 28 th day the design mix at preliminary test and work site shall be as per IS 456, SP 23 and SP 24. The water cement ratio shall be between 0.5 to 0.52. Additional water may be permitted only at the discretion of the ER. The slump shall be 25 mm to 35 mm depending upon the location and type of Work. Higher slump with use of plasticizers shall be permitted.

### [S049.U5] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE
- C. Design Mix And Trial Mixes
1. The Contractor shall submit the mix designs that he proposes to use at site to the ER for review at least 5 weeks in advance of planned use, The mix design shall also give basic details, when tested according to Is 1199 and IS 2386 - Part III, such as.
- a. Slump
- b. Vee - Bee Test

### [S049.U6] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > C. Design Mix And Trial Mixes
- c. Bleeding
- d. Cement required for one cubic meter of concrete
- e. Compacting factor
2. On receipt of this, the ER may immediately order a work site test to be performed before the final approval. This shall be done with mixer and materials actually being used at site.
3. 5 cubes shall be taken from each of the 3 batches to test the mix. Cubes shall be cast, stored, cured, transported and tested per IS 516. The test may be carried out at site or laboratory as approved by the ER.

### [S049.U13] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > D. Mixing Of Concrete
- a. Excessive mixing requiring the addition of water to preserve the required consistency shall not be permitted. Mix concrete to a consistency which can be readily placed without segregation.
- b. Equip mixers with a device for measuring and dispensing admixtures. When required, the slump of concrete may be increased prior to placement by the use of a high range water reducing admixture.

### [S049.U15] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > D. Mixing Of Concrete
6. Retempering: No water shall be added to the mix after the initial batching operation. Concrete which is placed after the unauthorized addition of water is subject to removal.
7. When required, the slump of concrete as delivered to the site may be increased prior to placement by the use of a high range water reducing admixture. Dosage of superplasticizer shall be within the guidelines established by the manufacturer and agreed to by the ER. Alternative Mix Design Reports with the recommended site dosage(s) of superplasticizer shall be submitted prior to use.

### [S049.U16] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > D. Mixing Of Concrete
8. The placing temperature of concrete shall not be more than 34 o C. If it is more, the ER may order addition of ice or chilled water to the concrete at no additional cost to the Employer. Also the Contractor shall take the following precautions:
- a. Mixers and weight batches shall be painted with white colour
- b. Aggregate storing bins shall not be exposed to the Sun.
- c. Water shall be sprinkled on aggregates well before concreting to keep the temperature low.

### [S050.U1] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > E. Shrinkage cracks
1. Concreting shall be avoided in very warm weather, if necessary, it shall be covered with dampened Hessian within 2 hours of placing of concrete.
2. To achieve good results the concrete shall be immediately covered with a plastic sheet and not exposed to any direct wind contact.

### [S053.U1] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > H. Construction joints > 1. In large pours, it is practically not possible to carry on concr...
1. In large pours, it is practically not possible to carry on concreting continuously. Hence construction joints shall be provided. Location of construction joint shall be submitted by the Contractor for approval of the ER. Such joints shall be kept to a minimum. The joints shall be at places where shear forces are nil or minimum and these shall be straight and at right angles to the direction of the main reinforcement.

### [S053.U4] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > H. Construction joints > 1. In large pours, it is practically not possible to carry on concr...
4. For vertical joints neat cement slurry shall be applied on the surface just before concreting. For horizontal joints, the surface shall be covered with a layer of mortar about 10 to 15 mm thick composed of cement and sand in the same ratio as the cement and sand in the concrete mix. This layer of cement slurry shall be freshly mixed and applied just before concreting.

### [S053.U6] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > H. Construction joints
- J. Waterstops:
1. Self-Expanding Strip Waterstops: Install in construction joints and at other locations as indicated, according to manufacturer's written instructions and recommendations, bonding or mechanically fastening and firmly pressing into place. Install in longest lengths practicable.
- K. Embedded Items and Inserts:
1. Accurately set anchorage devices by line and transit, and coordinate the locating of anchorage devices to be set for the accommodation of the Work of other trades.
2. Locate anchor bolts as shown on the Drawings and on shop drawings. Obtain necessary templates from the mechanical trades as required for the proper setting of anchor bolts and other items for mechanical equipment, as required.
3. Assist other trades in the installation of piping, pipe sleeves, conduit and similar items where items are to be installed in concrete. Provide frames to securely hold anchor bolts and anchorage devices in place during construction, and take care that no

displacement occurs during the pouring of concrete. Under this Section furnish and set items not furnished by other trades using approved standard type items suitable for their intended purpose.

4. Inserts and embedments shall located as shown in the Drawings and shall be protected from weather and damage in course of the construction.

### [S054.U2] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > L. Openings
- M. Filling-In: Fill in block-outs, holes and openings left in concrete structures for passage of Work by other trades, unless otherwise shown or directed, after Work of other trades is in place. Mix, place, and cure concrete as herein specified, to blend with in-place construction. Use non-shrink materials or admixtures as appropriate. Provide other miscellaneous concrete filling shown or required to complete the Work.
